samples.summary: Read-only image clicks now stop propagation, so the context menu's document-level outside-click closer never fires — and this PR is what makes that menu openable in read-only
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2609) lost its `if (readOnly) return;` and, on an image hit, calls `e.stopPropagation()` / `e.stopImmediatePropagation()` (editor.ts:2666-2667) from a *capture*-phase listener on the container (editor.ts:2683). That prevents the event ever reaching the bubble-phase `document.addEventListener("mousedown", handleClick)` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:126 (and the same pattern at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.tsx:103). Before this change the read-only context menu could not open at all (`hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly` bailed at line 80); this PR both opens it (`!readOnly || hasSelection`) and makes image mousedowns swallow the dismissal, so a viewer who right-clicks selected text and then clicks an image is left with an open, orphaned menu over a document whose selection has changed. The fix belongs on the new code — the image branch could let the mousedown reach `document` (it already only needs to stop the TextEditor's container listener), or the menu could also close on the editor's selection change.

samples.summary: Skipping TextEditor.handleMouseDown for read-only image clicks removes more than the link bookkeeping the diff compensated for — drag-selection can no longer start on an image for a viewer
samples.evidence: The new read-only path in `handleImageMouseDown` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2666-2667) suppresses `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` entirely; the diff hand-restores only `readOnlyPendingLinkHref` via `recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse`. The rest of that handler is not restored: the drag-selection arming (`isMouseDown`, anchor placement and the `document.addEventListener('mouseup', ...)` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1714) never runs, so a viewer who presses on an image and drags outward no longer selects the surrounding text — behaviour they had before this PR, since read-only image mousedowns previously fell straight through to the TextEditor. Editable mode already had this limitation, so the regression is confined to read-only mounts.

samples.summary: EditorAPI.selectImageAt now steals DOM focus, and its interface doc comment still describes the old side-effect-free contract
samples.evidence: `selectImageAt` is routed through the new `selectImageInline` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1256-1261), which calls `textEditorRef?.focus()`. The public interface doc at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:311-317 still says only "Programmatically mark the image at (blockId, offset) as the selected image… No-op if the offset does not point at an image inline" — nothing about moving keyboard focus to the hidden textarea. Any caller that selects an image from its own UI (the context-menu / image-options flows the comment anticipates) will now have focus yanked out of its popover or input. The design doc (docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:263-272) does record the focus call, so only the API-level contract comment is out of step.

samples.summary: imageKeyHandler now consumes bare modifier keydowns and Cmd/Ctrl+C/X, so handleKeyDown's pre-switch bookkeeping is skipped for those events while an image is selected
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.handleKeyDown` returns immediately when `imageKeyHandler` returns true (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:865). The new branches return `true` for `Meta`/`Control`/`Shift`/`Alt`/… and for mod+C/mod+X (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2382-2403), so two pieces of out-of-diff bookkeeping below that point never run while an image is selected: the stale-cursor recovery at text-editor.ts:871 and the software-Hangul flush at text-editor.ts:915 (which explicitly flushes on `mod`). Practical impact is small — `shiftHeld` is still updated at line 850 and the copy path does not mutate — but a Hangul composition left unflushed across a Ctrl+C with an image selected is a real, if narrow, difference from every other key.

finding.summary: Remote-change path never clears the image selection, so the new "any offset-shifting mutation clears it" invariant is bypassed by every collaborator edit
finding.evidence: The diff establishes the rule that any mutation shifting offsets must call `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` (editor.ts:1288 and its ~15 call sites). The remote path is the one mutation source that never does: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:378-393` (`store.onRemoteChange`) calls `editor.getDoc().refresh()`, `editor.restoreLocalCursor(...)`, `editor.validateCursorPosition()` and `editor.render()` — none of which touches `selectedImage` (`restoreLocalCursor` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3917-3931 only moves the cursor and sets the selection range; `validateCursorPosition` at editor.ts:979-987 likewise). A peer inserting or deleting text before the selected image shifts the `(blockId, offset)` coordinate the selection is expressed in. The hardening added in this diff only protects against the block/inline being *gone*: `deleteSelectedImageInline` and `imageSelectionProvider` re-validate with `findImageAtOffset`, which merely asserts that *some* image sits at that offset — so where a remote edit slides a different image onto the slot (exactly the `blockWithTwoImages` scenario the new tests use for local mutations), Cmd/Ctrl+X or Delete removes/copies the wrong image, and the overlay is painted around it beforehand. Fix belongs at the docs-view remote handler (call `editor.clearImageSelection()` there, the same seam the find bar was given at docs-find-bar.tsx:124) or inside `restoreLocalCursor`.

verdict.reason: The invariant is real and the remote path bypasses it. editor.ts:1263-1294 defines clearImageSelectionForMutation() with the explicit rule that any offset-shifting mutation must clear the (blockId, offset) image selection, and ~15 in-module call sites plus the exported EditorAPI.clearImageSelection (editor.ts:3840) enforce it. A repo-wide grep for clearImageSelection finds exactly two production frontend call sites, both in docs-find-bar.tsx (124, 133). The sole remote-change handler — docs-view.tsx:378-394, the only assignment of store.onRemoteChange, fired for every 'remote-change' event at yorkie-doc-store.ts:576-581 — calls getDoc().refresh(), restoreLocalCursor, publishResolvedLocalCursor, validateCursorPosition and render, none of which touch selectedImage: restoreLocalCursor (editor.ts:3921-3935) only moves the caret and sets the range; validateCursorPosition (editor.ts:979-987) only relocates the caret when the block itself is gone; render (editor.ts:1908-1911) merely looks up rects by `${blockId}:${offset}` with no identity check; Document.refresh (model/document.ts:123) has no selection hook. The re-validation added in the diff is offset-shaped, not identity-shaped: deleteSelectedImageInline (editor.ts:2312-2333) and imageSelectionProvider (editor.ts:2337-2348) only require that some image sits at the stored offset, so a peer edit that shifts another image into that slot makes Delete/Cmd+X act on, and the overlay paint around, the wrong image. I found no counterexample anywhere — no alternate remote-side clear under another name, no clearing inside the store, the Doc, or the render path.
